notes: Axis Naval Convoy Air Distance Chart (printed as 56.18, a case number the rules index does not list; the chart sits under the 37.42 Land Distance Chart on rules page jp2 71). Each lane is a fixed origin and destination (56.11-56.12); the Axis may not make new pairs. Its number is the Convoy Route column of the Simple Axis Naval Convoy Bombing Chart (axis-convoy-bombing.json, 32.66).

Read twice: the archive.org scan (jp2 71) and the community converted rules PDF (scan:discord:CampaignNorthAfrica - converted.pdf:p72, rendered at 200 dpi): 0 of 41 cells differ. The djvu OCR text agrees on every value it kept.

distances: hexes from planes in the Sicily, Italy or Crete box, any Malta hex, or the North African rally point to the lane. A plane from a North African air facility needs range for its facility to a rally point plus that rally point's figure (41.62, 42.52). null is the chart's dash (lane 1 from Crete).

Opening: lanes 4 and 5 (from Greece) from the second Game-Turn of May 1941, Game-Turn 32 (56.14; calendar.json). Lane 1 ends at Bizerta in the Tunisia box, which cannot be used before Game-Turn 35 (June I 1941) and then only once the Axis rolls 12 on two dice in a Game-Turn (55.17). So in 1940 and early 1941 only lanes 2, 3 and 6 are open, which is what Graziani's Offensive repeats (60.37).
A convoy whose destination port the Commonwealth captures before it sails is cancelled (56.15); a lane has no tonnage limit of its own (56.17).
